components.label: Seed submitter
components.responsibility: Submit URLs and a bounded crawl scope.

components.label: Crawler boundary
components.responsibility: Discover, fetch and persist pages within policy.

components.label: Durable host frontier
components.responsibility: Own pending URLs, host leases, attempt state and transactional outbox.

components.label: Fetch/parse worker
components.responsibility: Process one leased URL with bounded network and parser work.

components.label: URL canonicalizer and admission
components.responsibility: Normalize only semantics-preserving URL parts; deduplicate atomically by crawl ID and canonical URL.

components.label: Robots and destination guard
components.responsibility: Check robots, scheme, resolved IPs and each redirect; deny private/reserved destinations.

components.label: Host scheduler
components.responsibility: Allocate per-origin permits in durable shared state with fencing tokens.

components.label: Immutable response store
components.responsibility: Persist response bytes and attempt metadata before acknowledging fetch.

components.label: Document index
components.responsibility: Upsert by crawl identity, canonical URL and document version.

components.label: Fetch workers
components.responsibility: Only network and response persistence; no expensive extraction on this stage.

components.label: Parse workers
components.responsibility: Run bounded parsing on persisted objects without re-fetching.

components.label: Durable parse queue
components.responsibility: Deliver persisted body references at least once.

components.label: Lease recovery sweeper
components.responsibility: Requeue expired attempts with a new fencing token and bounded retry policy.

components.label: Index/discovery outbox
components.responsibility: Dispatch document and link events durably; mark each intent complete after acknowledged handling.

components.label: Unified crawl scheduler
components.responsibility: Own admission, host scheduling and scope budgets through durable transactions.

requirements.text: Schedule URLs with durable leases, retries and per-origin politeness.
Apply robots policy, URL normalization and network destination checks before every request and redirect.
Deduplicate admission without collapsing semantically different URLs; idempotently store and index fetched content.
Recover after worker failure with bounded outstanding work and observable terminal outcomes.

problem.scope: Crawl public HTTP(S) pages with explicit robots policy, bounded fetches and durable progress. Compare a host-partitioned fetch/parse worker with separate fetch and parse pipelines. URL deduplication is not content equivalence.

provenance.note: Authored interview preparation. Technical references support mechanisms, not the claim that a company asked this question.

references.supports: Robots matching and retrieval error semantics.
references.title: Robots Exclusion Protocol

references.supports: Reconciliation of durable progress after partial failures.
references.title: Durable controller pattern

acceptanceCases.given: Two workers discover the same URL and another URL with a distinct query value.
acceptanceCases.then: Admit one copy of the exact canonical URL and preserve the semantically distinct URL.

acceptanceCases.given: An allowed public URL redirects to loopback or resolves to a private IP.
acceptanceCases.then: Refuse the private destination before sending the HTTP request.
acceptanceCases.when: Follow the redirect or reconnect after DNS changes.

acceptanceCases.given: Policy disallows a path and a stale cached robots document exists.
acceptanceCases.then: Apply explicit RFC-compatible refresh/error policy; do not assume stale permission forever.
acceptanceCases.when: Try to fetch after the cache policy expires.

acceptanceCases.then: Shared permits enforce the configured request-start interval and concurrency ceiling.

acceptanceCases.given: Attempt A expires and attempt B is leased.
acceptanceCases.then: Fence A from completing B’s work; retry policy remains bounded and observable.
acceptanceCases.when: A later completes while B is processing.

acceptanceCases.given: A body and discovery intents commit but the delivery acknowledgement is lost.
acceptanceCases.then: Upsert the same document version and admit each discovered URL once.

guarantees: Attempt fencing protects progress; host politeness also needs conservative handling of uncertain in-flight calls.

assumptions: Per-origin request starts are serialized or budgeted in shared durable state.
A timed-out worker can still have an in-flight network request; leases cannot recall packets.
solutions.chooseWhen: A simpler crawler can process bounded pages inline within each host lease.

stages.explanation: Begin with seed input and a coarse crawler. Crawl scope, depth and total work have explicit ceilings. [A crawler](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Web_crawler) chooses which URLs to fetch and when. Scheduling must balance discovery with per-site limits, while canonicalization and duplicate checks prevent repeated or unbounded work. Consider this case: Two workers discover the same URL and another URL with a distinct query value.
invariants: Crawl scope, depth and total work have explicit ceilings.
stages.question: Which URLs and budgets belong to this crawl?
stages.reason: Begin with seed input and a coarse crawler.
stages.title: Define scope and a seed path

stages.explanation: Expand the crawler into durable pending work and a worker. Deleting pending work before a durable result is forbidden. [A crawler](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Web_crawler) chooses which URLs to fetch and when. Scheduling must balance discovery with per-site limits, while canonicalization and duplicate checks prevent repeated or unbounded work. Consider this case: Attempt A expires and attempt B is leased. A later completes while B is processing.
invariants: Deleting pending work before a durable result is forbidden.
stages.question: Where does work survive a crash?
stages.reason: Expand the crawler into durable pending work and a worker.
stages.title: Separate frontier and execution

stages.explanation: Make URL canonicalization and atomic admission visible. Do not drop query parameters or reorder them without a site-specific semantic rule. [Backpressure](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Flow_control_%28data%29) prevents producers from outrunning the next component indefinitely. The design must choose whether excess work waits, is rejected, or is dropped with an explicit outcome. Consider this case: Two workers discover the same URL and another URL with a distinct query value.
invariants: Do not drop query parameters or reorder them without a site-specific semantic rule.
stages.question: Can normalization accidentally remove a distinct page?
stages.reason: Make URL canonicalization and atomic admission visible.
stages.title: Add semantics-preserving admission

stages.explanation: Guard each fetch and redirect, including DNS results and connection destination. Robots controls crawling policy; it is not authentication or permission to access private networks. [A crawler](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Web_crawler) chooses which URLs to fetch and when. Scheduling must balance discovery with per-site limits, while canonicalization and duplicate checks prevent repeated or unbounded work.
invariants: Robots controls crawling policy; it is not authentication or permission to access private networks.
stages.question: What prevents internal-network requests and disallowed paths?
stages.reason: Guard each fetch and redirect, including DNS results and connection destination.
stages.title: Enforce robots and destination safety

stages.explanation: Use a shared host scheduler instead of process-local delays. A lease expiry may cause overlapping attempts; bound duplicate load and fence stale completion. [A directed acyclic graph](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Directed_acyclic_graph) expresses work that depends on earlier results. A scheduler must track completed dependencies and distinguish logical tasks from retry attempts before releasing downstream work.
invariants: A lease expiry may cause overlapping attempts; bound duplicate load and fence stale completion.
stages.question: What if several workers share a target host?
stages.reason: Use a shared host scheduler instead of process-local delays.
stages.title: Coordinate host politeness

stages.explanation: Store immutable bodies; make the independent parsing boundary explicit when selected. Fetch completion records and body references must commit before parse dispatch is acknowledged. [Transaction guarantees](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/ACID) describe which changes become visible together and what survives failure. They must be tied to explicit storage behavior rather than inferred from a successful API call.
invariants: Fetch completion records and body references must commit before parse dispatch is acknowledged.
stages.question: Can parsing retry without fetching the network again?
stages.reason: Store immutable bodies; make the independent parsing boundary explicit when selected.
stages.title: Persist responses before inline parsing

stages.explanation: Add retry recovery and a transactional outbox for derived work. A stale attempt cannot mark a newer attempt complete. [Transaction guarantees](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/ACID) describe which changes become visible together and what survives failure. They must be tied to explicit storage behavior rather than inferred from a successful API call. Consider this case: Attempt A expires and attempt B is leased.
invariants: A stale attempt cannot mark a newer attempt complete.
Persist immutable body bytes first, then atomically commit the frontier result metadata and link/index outbox intents before acknowledgement; orphaned body objects are safe to collect.
stages.question: What if a worker dies between storage and publishing discovered URLs?
stages.reason: Add retry recovery and a transactional outbox for derived work.
stages.title: Recover leases and durable publication

stages.explanation: Unify budget and scheduling decisions under one durable transaction boundary. Restarting a scheduler never resets the durable crawl budget. [A directed acyclic graph](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Directed_acyclic_graph) expresses work that depends on earlier results. A scheduler must track completed dependencies and distinguish logical tasks from retry attempts before releasing downstream work. Consider this case: Two workers discover the same URL and another URL with a distinct query value.
invariants: Restarting a scheduler never resets the durable crawl budget.

operations.reason: One owner checks scope, admission identity and host capacity rather than competing process-local counters.

stages.question: Can admission and per-host scheduling race against the crawl budget?
stages.reason: Unify budget and scheduling decisions under one durable transaction boundary.
stages.title: Merge scheduling authority

solutions.title: Host-partitioned fetch/parse workers
tradeoffs: Slow parsing ties up worker capacity even after network I/O completes.
A single worker implementation is simpler to deploy and trace.
